correctness.rationale: The source Hamiltonian is quarter-turn invariant and decomposes over quasi-momentum fibers. Rotation therefore maps the k fiber unitarily to the Rk fiber, so their lowest energies agree. Twice differentiating the exact scalar identity gives orthogonal conjugacy of Hessians; inversion gives the same covariance for nonsingular mass tensors. For any symmetric 2-by-2 matrix A, A+RAR^T=(tr A)I exactly. The proof keeps C2 regularity and Hessian invertibility explicit and does not infer an infinite statement from finite computation.

value.rationale: The source makes the dressed-pair dispersion and tensor mass central to transport and to its effective-mass discussion. The two cuprate-motivated valleys are natural symmetry partners already used in the earlier model literature. The result shows that arbitrary anisotropy of either single valley cannot survive an equal-weight two-valley quadratic average, uniformly across the generalized exchange/Hubbard parameters and including the hard-core limit. This separates internal/pairing anisotropy from symmetry-protected center-of-mass quadratic isotropy and is a structural lemma rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
